This is a really important post from @TindakV2 (again, you should all be following them, election mania coming soon!).

We always say that election boundaries should "respect local ties". And then we use district/PBT boundaries as a proxy for local ties.

However, those district/PBT boundaries are often hugely problematic, and have not shifted to respond to population changes.

In fact, in an ideal world, electoral boundaries would give you the best sense of how to subdivide a country, because by law they can change every 8 years.

Besides the excellent example of Padawan which Tindak gave, my other favourite example is Kuala Lumpur itself.

The boundary dividing Selangor and KL is frankly incoherent. It made a lot more sense in 1974, for the population/addresses at the time.

Over 50 years, the population has sprawled and shifted, but the boundary remains the same.
